title: Using CLAUDE.md files: Customizing Claude Code for your codebase
tldr: This blog post introduces the use of `CLAUDE.md` files for granular customization of Claude Code's behavior within specific code repositories. Developers can define project-specific instructions, constraints, and context to fine-tune Claude's agentic coding assistant for improved relevance and accuracy.

title: How to create Skills: Key steps, limitations, and examples
tldr: This guide details the process for developers to create custom 'Skills' for Claude, enabling the model to perform specific, predefined actions or access external tools. It covers implementation steps, outlines current limitations, and provides practical examples for extending Claude's capabilities programmatically.

title: Structured outputs on the Claude Developer Platform
tldr: The Claude Developer Platform now supports structured outputs, allowing developers to constrain Claude's responses to specific JSON schemas or other defined formats. This enhancement significantly improves the reliability and predictability of integrating LLM outputs into downstream applications and workflows.

title: Skills explained: How Skills compares to prompts, Projects, MCP, and subagents
tldr: This article provides a detailed technical comparison of Claude's new 'Skills' feature against existing methodologies like prompts, Projects, Multi-Competency Path (MCP), and subagents. It elucidates the distinct operational paradigms and integration points for each concept, clarifying how Skills offer a modular approach to extending agent capabilities.

title: Migrate MLflow tracking servers to Amazon SageMaker AI with serverless MLflow
tldr: This post details the technical process of migrating existing MLflow tracking servers to Amazon SageMaker AI's new serverless MLflow offering. It outlines the architectural benefits of reduced operational overhead and enhanced scalability for MLOps workflows, ensuring seamless experiment tracking and model management in a fully managed environment.

title: Build an AI-powered website assistant with Amazon Bedrock
tldr: This engineering blog provides a step-by-step guide for constructing an AI-powered website assistant using Amazon Bedrock, leveraging its foundation models and agentic capabilities. It details the integration of RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) patterns with knowledge bases to provide accurate, context-aware responses, and outlines deployment on AWS infrastructure.
